content.title: Is Chicago Fire new tonight? No, NBC airs repeat episode instead - Art Threat
content.text: Show summary Hide summary 🔥 Quick Facts Why NBC Pulled New Episodes Tonight What’s Airing Instead of New Episodes Complete March 25 One Chicago Rerun Schedule Mark April 1 for New Episode 16 Should You Watch Tonight’s Reruns, Or Wait for New Episodes? Sources Chicago Fire fans hoping for new drama tonight are in for a disappointment. NBC is airing repeat episodes instead of fresh episodes on March 25, 2026. The good news? New episodes return in April. 🔥 Quick Facts Tonight’s Episode: Rerun of season 14, episode 2, “Primary Search,” airs at 9 p.m. ET No New Episodes: Chicago Fire, Med, and PD all going into reruns on March 25 Return Date: New episode 16 premieres April 1, 2026 at 8 p.m. CT Peacock Option: All reruns available on Peacock streaming service Why NBC Pulled New Episodes Tonight NBC decided to air encore episodes on March 25 rather than push forward with fresh content. The network reached a point in the season where spacing out remaining episodes became necessary before the shows wrap in late May. No official reason was announced, but scheduling reruns mid-season helps NBC manage its programming calendar strategically. Chicago Fire, Chicago Med, and Chicago PD all felt the same programming shift simultaneously. This isn’t an extended hiatus like the Winter Olympics break from earlier this year. Fans won’t wait weeks for new content, making this just a one-week pause in the action. The reprieve gives writers and production teams final breathing room before the season rush concludes. What’s Airing Instead of New Episodes Rather than leaving viewers empty-handed, NBC is throwing back to earlier season episodes. Chicago Fire fans will get season 14, episode 2, titled “Primary Search,” at 9 p.m. ET. This early-season episode reintroduced audiences to Sal Vasquez, the firehouse’s newest recruit who quickly became beloved despite early uncertainty about his character arc. The episode captures Vasquez striving to prove his worth at Station 51 while Violet and Novak investigate a disturbing case. Meanwhile, Herrmann battles to maintain Molly’s Bar profitability. Fans worried about losing Vasquez should use tonight as a reminder of his compelling introduction to the firehouse. Complete March 25 One Chicago Rerun Schedule Show Time Episode Chicago Med 8 p.m. ET Season 11, Episode 2: “A Game of Inches” Chicago Fire 9 p.m. ET Season 14, Episode 2: “Primary Search” Chicago PD 10 p.m. ET Season 13, Episode 2: “Open Wounds” “Although there will not be any new episodes of Chicago Fire, Chicago Med, and Chicago PD airing on March 25, NBC will at least be airing reruns.” — One Chicago Center, Entertainment News Source Mark April 1 for New Episode 16 Next Wednesday, April 1, 2026, fresh episodes return to NBC. Chicago Fire’s new episode 16 will premiere at 8 p.m. CT according to official NBC press releases. That’s when the story picks up after three weeks of new episode delays scattered throughout March. Fans can watch live on NBC or stream next-day episodes on Peacock the following morning for commercial-free viewing. All three shows, Chicago Fire, Chicago Med, and Chicago PD, will resume their normal Wednesday night schedule with simultaneous premieres. This marks the final stretch before the shows conclude their seasons in late May. Viewers frustrated by tonight’s reruns have just seven days to wait for the narrative to advance. Should You Watch Tonight’s Reruns, Or Wait for New Episodes? For devoted fans comfortable revisiting early-season episodes, tonight offers value. “Primary Search” introduced important character development for Vasquez and set up storylines that evolved throughout the season. Viewers who missed this episode or want nostalgia will appreciate the throwback. However, those exclusively following current storylines can safely skip tonight and return April 1 without confusion. Peacock offers an alternative for anyone unwilling to watch commercials on NBC. Every episode airing tonight is available on the streaming service, making it possible to enjoy the reruns without ads during prime time. This flexibility gives fans complete control over their viewing experience while NBC manages seasonal scheduling.
